title: Live Simulation Prober for Backwards Compatibility and KV-Cache Priming
creator: Imani Thompson
description: Goal: build a live-simulation prober that exercises multiple API surface permutations (streaming variants, function/tool calling formats, structured/NDJSON outputs, and compatibility shims) against current and previous runtime wire-protocols. The harness will: 1) replay representative traffic collected from sanitized telemetry and synthetic golden seeds; 2) vary protocol parameters (chunk sizes, partial JSON boundaries, interleaved toolcall events, function-call metadata encoding) to find edgecases; 3) prime and validate KV-cache behaviours across sequences to ensure cache reuse does not change structured-output fidelity; 4) produce behavioral fingerprints (hashed canonical output traces) and score diffs against accepted baselines; 5) run quick smoke checks in PRs and deeper nightly regression runs in CI. Success criteria: CI runs must detect regressions for streaming order, partial-response reconstruction, function-call argument fidelity, and structured-output schema drift. Runner language: Go for low-latency socket harness + Python for fuzz scenario composition and analyser. Integration points: CI job gating for runtime and API-shim changes, dashboard alerts in Console, and automated PR comments linking failing trace diffs.
